simplifications.text: Each layout was drawn on one lot. On another lot it is placed as drawn, moved or mirrored to fit inside the lot and its yards; it is not re-planned for that lot.
"Needs rezoning (tested as if I-2)" means the lot was tested with the I-2 district’s limits (height, floor area, yards), not its own zone’s. Rezoning is a council decision.

source.citation: City of Vancouver Zoning and Development By-law, I-2 District Schedule. 2026.

simplifications.text: "Needs 2 lots joined" checks only the combined lot’s shape and yards. Ownership, the buildings on the lots and the cost of joining them are not checked.
Public corridor walls are fire separations, but they need no fire-resistance rating in a sprinklered storey, so the tool does not draw them.

source.citation: National Building Code of Canada 2020, Div. B 3.3.1.4.(3).

simplifications.text: Lots in the City’s designated floodplain are flagged. Buildings are not raised to the flood construction level in the drawings, and on lots tested as if I-2 the flood check does not run.

source.citation: City of Vancouver Open Data, Designated floodplain.

simplifications.text: Interior doors are not drawn. Rooms connect where they share a wall; only outside doors are placed.
Some zone edges have short jogs, and a few small support rooms sit apart from their main room. These are drawing simplifications, not design decisions.
